Summarise a change table

Source: R/yoy_output.R
yoysmry.Rd

Collapses a period-over-period change table from yoy into one row per series (or one row per group when yoy() was called with by). Each row gives the first and last observed periods, the total change between them, the compound annual growth rate, and how many period-to-period changes went up, went down or stayed flat. Use it to report the whole span of a series in one line next to the detailed table.

Usage

yoysmry(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
yoysmry(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_yoy'
yoysmry(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An rmbl_yoy object returned by yoy.

...

Further arguments for methods; not used.

Value

A data frame with one row per series or group and columns: the by columns (character), when yoy() had by; from, to (the first and last observed period, same type as the period column); first, last (numeric values at those periods); totalpct, cagrpct (numeric, percent); periods (integer, observed periods); up, down, flat (integer counts of period-to-period changes).

Details

Rows whose value is missing are dropped before the summary, and the remaining rows are sorted by period, text periods in the order yoy() read them (its prd and prdord). Periods with no order (text yoy() could not read, an unordered factor) have no first or last: from, to, first, last, totalpct and cagrpct are then NA, with a warning saying why. With \(v_1\) the first and \(v_T\) the last observed value, the total change is $$100 (v_T / v_1 - 1)$$ and, with \(s = (T - 1) / \mathrm{lag}\) steps of length lag, $$100 \left( (v_T / v_1)^{1/s} - 1 \right).$$ Both are NA when \(v_1 \le 0\), because a growth rate out of zero does not exist; cagrpct is also NA for a single period. "Annual" in CAGR assumes one period is a year; for monthly or quarterly data read it as the compound rate per lag periods.

The up, down and flat counts are taken from the percent-change column (pctchg, or ppchg for units = "percent"). A change out of a zero base has no percent change and is not counted in any of the three. A group with no non-missing value gives a row of NA with periods = 0.

Anything other than a yoy() result is refused with the error “object must be a yoy() result”.

See also

yoy, yoypals.

Examples

# one series
d <- data.frame(year = 2018:2023, n = c(120, 131, 98, 140, 155, 149))
yoysmry(yoy(d, value = "n", prd = "year"))
#> ╭── Year-over-year summary ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Series  1                                                            │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   from  to    first  last  totalpct  cagrpct  periods  up  down  flat  │
#> │   ----  ----  -----  ----  --------  -------  -------  --  ----  ----  │
#> │   2018  2023    120   149     24.17    4.424        6   3     2     0  │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   totalpct is the change from the first period to the last and cagrpct │
#> │   the compound rate per step; up, down and flat count the changes from │
#> │   one period to the next.                                              │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# one row per group; a zero base gives no percent change
g <- data.frame(year = rep(2019:2022, 2), unit = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),
                n = c(10, 12, 0, 15, 5, 7, 6, 9))
yoysmry(yoy(g, value = "n", prd = "year", by = "unit"))
#> ╭── Year-over-year summary ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Series  2                                                            │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   unit  from  to    first  last  totalpct  cagrpct  periods  up  down  │
#> │   ----  ----  ----  -----  ----  --------  -------  -------  --  ----  │
#> │   A     2019  2022     10    15        50    14.47        4   1     1  │
#> │   B     2019  2022      5     9        80    21.64        4   2     1  │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   unit  flat                                                           │
#> │   ----  ----                                                           │
#> │   A        0                                                           │
#> │   B        0                                                           │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   totalpct is the change from the first period to the last and cagrpct │
#> │   the compound rate per step; up, down and flat count the changes from │
#> │   one period to the next.                                              │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# anything that is not a yoy() result is refused
try(yoysmry(d))
#> Error : `object` must be a yoy() result, not data.frame
